rules.statement: The prohibition on alienation to an outsider is personal and only applies to the immediate devisees, not their lawful issue.
rules.supporting_quote: "But prohibitions which are not nude, but binding, appear to fall under one of two general classes, to wit, (i) personal, (ii) real prohibitions- (i) 'A prohibition is personal when. a testator interdicts certain persons, by name or as a class from making alienation; for example, if he says, ' I prohibit Titus or my heir or legatee from alienating the land. ' When a prohibition is in this way imposed upon a person, it applies only to the person prohibited, and does not go beyond him.'"
